data.name: Perpetua
data.gender_notes: Perpetua is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word 'perpetuus' meaning everlasting, continuous. In early Christian history, Saint Perpetua was a noblewoman who, along with Saint Felicity, was put to death for her faith. She is now recognized as a martyr and patron saint of many causes. The name Perpetua carries the meaning “Everlasting, continuous” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Perpetua usually hope their child will grow to embody everlasting, continuous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of steadfast faith and enduring spirit
data.etymology: Perpetua belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Everlasting, continuous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Perpetua total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Perpetua is a significant historical figure in North Africa's Christian history, representing the bravery and unwavering faith of early Christian martyrs persecuted for their beliefs.
data.spiritual_significance: Her name symbolizes the eternal nature of faith and the continuous journey of the soul towards God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Perpetua: Eternal and unchanging one. A symbol of enduring faith and steadfastness. Her name embodies the unwavering nature of the Christian belief.

historical_references.reference: Perpetua was a young noblewoman who, along with her slave Felicitas and two other catechumens, Saturus and Revocatus, were martyred in Carthage, North Africa, during the reign of Emperor Septimius Severus (AD 193-211).
historical_references.context: The martyrdom of Perpetua and her companions took place during the persecution of Christians under Septimius Severus. The account of their martyrdom was written by Perpetua herself, in a remarkable first-person narrative.

historical_references.reference: Perpetua was a prominent Christian matron in Carthage, who was martyred during the reign of Emperor Diocletian (AD 284-305) in AD 258, along with her slave Felicity and her catechumen son, Flaminianus.
historical_references.context: Perpetua and Felicity were two women who were arrested and martyred during the Great Persecution of Diocletian. Perpetua was a wealthy, married woman with a young son. Her husband, who was not a Christian, did not intervene to save her. The account of their martyrdom was written by an eyewitness.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Perpetua continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Perpetua from Rome, Italy embodies the meaning of Perpetua - "Everlasting, continuous". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
